summary.headline: Apollo Pipes Q2 FY27 volume rose 13% YoY to 24,501 tonnes and EBITDA recovered to Rs 11.5 crore at a 3.7% margin, while the company entered ceramic tiles.
summary.overview: Management said market conditions improved gradually in Q2 FY27 as polymer price volatility eased from Q1 levels, helped by government measures on PVC resin imports and duty exemptions. Revenue grew 31% YoY to Rs 309.6 crore and EBITDA recovered from Rs 3 crore in Q1 to Rs 11.5 crore, though margins remain below target. The company entered ceramic tiles through the acquisition of a 76% stake in Mazini Tiles, a Morbi-based business, and plans a 2,40,000-tonne to 2,80,000-tonne capacity expansion funded from internal cash flow. The Kisan brand remains loss-making and management has set a 6 to 9 month break-even target for it.

segments.name: Plumbing pipes (Apollo brand, standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA around Rs 7,000 per tonne; management expects H2 improvement as volumes ramp. UPVC is 45% of sales, CPVC 15-20%, PPR under 5%; the balance is water tanks, window profiles, UPVC and HDPE pipes.

segments.name: Kisan brand
segments.commentary: Loss-making, with EBITDA per tonne stated at a loss of around Rs 3,700. Management targets break-even within 6 to 9 months and Rs 4,000 to 7,000 per tonne thereafter.

segments.name: Ceramic tiles (Mazini Tiles, Morbi)
segments.commentary: New subsidiary entered in Q2 with a 76% stake in the first asset, bought at about 5x EV/EBITDA. Management targets a 15-20% ROCE and at least five assets, with a long-term ambition of Rs 1,000 crore revenue and a 10% ROCE-type return.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to be better than H1, with PVC prices stabilising and Q4 volume run-rate of about 30,000 tonnes.
Standalone EBITDA per tonne expected to recover toward Rs 10,000 over the next 3 to 4 years, helped by the South India plant (about Rs 3,000 per tonne spread improvement).
Long-term target: about Rs 3,000 crore plumbing revenue and Rs 1,000 crore ceramics revenue, with about 80% domestic and 20% export mix in ceramics.
Capacity to rise from 2,40,000 tonnes to 2,80,000 tonnes within two years, funded from internal cash flow without leveraging the balance sheet.
Rs 130 crore to be raised by selling two to three land parcels within 6 to 12 months to help fund the South India plant.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 2,40,000 tonnes; target 2,80,000 tonnes within two years.
Greenfield plant planned in South India (Tumkur area); land not yet acquired as of the call, with identification under way. Management said the project was delayed.
Varanasi plant commissioned, expected to ramp up in East and Central India at better margins.
Several small plants (under 5 to 30 acres) shut and volumes consolidated into larger new plants; management said the impact on volume is minimal.

Ceramics: Rs 200 crore equity raise announced; Apollo Pipes invested about Rs 100 crore, with roughly Rs 70 to 80 crore spent on the first asset. Rs 200 crore balance needed over 2 to 3 years, with a further Rs 100 to 200 crore for the wider ceramics programme.
demand_pricing: PVC price volatility eased in Q2 versus Q1; West Asia uncertainty continues to affect raw material prices. Government minimum import price on suspension grade PVC resin and withdrawal of duty exemptions supported the domestic market.
Industry was disrupted over the last two to three years by aggressive pricing and trading-led competition, which has hurt Kisan's premiumisation.
North India is about 70% of sales; management says Apollo pricing there is at par with the top players.
Management says Apollo has held roughly 4% market share, with industry volumes flat in the last two to three years.
Management says October run-rate was similar to Q2 levels, with channel inventory being kept very low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the logic for entering ceramic tiles, and how will the business scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tiles extend the building-materials category and offer a learning curve through acquisition of profitable units. The initial focus is contract manufacturing for existing brands in Morbi, a Rs 25,000 to 30,000 crore market, with branded tiles deferred. Target ROCE is 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for H2 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to improve from Q2's Rs 7,000 per tonne as volumes ramp, with the long-term aim of about Rs 10,000 per tonne EBITDA on a consolidated plumbing basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Kisan and its near-term recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kisan's recovery depends on industry dynamics. It targets break-even in 6 to 9 months, then a Rs 4,000 to 7,000 per tonne margin over the next 12 months. October run-rate was similar to Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why were smaller plants shut, and does the company own its land?
qa_highlights.answer: The plants were under 5 to 30 acres, and management said volumes were consolidated into larger, new plants with little logistics impact. All land is owned, and two to three parcels may be sold for about Rs 130 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ceramics business be funded, and will the company take majority stakes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will acquire majority stakes and run the assets itself. Rs 200 crore equity was raised and the balance will come from internal cash flows within 2 to 3 years, with no fund raise needed for the Rs 500 crore plan.

qa_highlights.question: What competitive advantage does Apollo have against Supreme and Finolex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to North India share of about 70% of sales, the Apollo brand in building materials, and the new plants in West, East and proposed South India as the basis for growth. Market share rose from zero to about 2.5% by 2021 and is now about 4%.

risks_watch: Kisan brand losses persist and break-even timeline of 6 to 9 months slips.
PVC price volatility from West Asia uncertainty; management assumes range-bound prices.
South India greenfield plant has not yet had land acquired, creating execution risk on the capacity target.
Ceramics acquisitions are new to the business; integration of Mazini and the wider Morbi pipeline is unproven.
Industry competition from trading-led players continues to constrain pricing and premiumisation.
Channel softness in early Q3 (October described as soft earlier in the quarter).
summary.management_tone: Management was confident about H2 and the margin recovery, but was cautious on Kisan and industry pricing, which it said is outside its control. Answers were often long and loosely structured, and several figures on Kisan, ceramics and capacity were restated or unclear.

We are on track to expand capacity to 28000 tons in the next two years from the current level of 2,40,000 tons and we remain committed to funding this expansion from internal cash flow without leveraging the balance sheet.
